blocks.text: The finding under the finding

content.value: The lead's mechanism is correct and I verified it at source. Content.Papers.reader_source/3 (api/lib/barkpark/content/papers.ex:60-138) classifies a paper's canonical blocks, and conflicting_html_cache?/4 re-renders those blocks with the CURRENT renderer and compares bytes against the stored body_html cache. Any difference becomes {:error, :ambiguous_source} and then HTTP 422. A renderer change therefore kills every unedited published paper that uses a touched block type.
But the byte-compare is doing DOUBLE DUTY, and that conflation is the real defect. It cannot tell apart two completely different situations:

items.value: DRIFT - the cache was rendered from THESE blocks by an OLDER renderer. Harmless. Self-healable. The blocks are canonical and re-rendering them is strictly safe.

DIVERGENCE - the stored HTML carries content the blocks do not (a legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list). Genuinely ambiguous. Preferring blocks here would silently destroy content.

content.value: The 422 was built for case 2. It fires on case 1 because a byte-compare has no way to ask which one it is looking at.

content[body_html_sv] is a render-version stamp written by SIX write sites (block_ops.ex:1313, writer.ex:529, sheets.ex:151, proposals.ex:151, doctrine_backfill.ex:493, composition_migration.ex:686). Render.body_html_render_version/0 declares it. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html re-renders any cache whose stamp lags. reader_source/3 never reads the stamp. It byte-compares instead.

blocks.title: The machinery to tell them apart already exists, and the read path ignores it

content.value: And the stamp itself is a hand-typed integer. api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render.ex:53 holds @body_html_render_version 3 above a comment instructing a human to bump it when render semantics change, and a second comment describing a manual deploy step: run mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html on guerrilla and prod after this wave merges. Four S-tier pdrender rounds landed on 07-18 (#4126, #4140, #4192) and a status-manifest change on 07-19 (#4394). Nobody bumped it. Nobody ran the sweep.

A version a human must remember to bump is not a version - it is a wish. The cache recorded WHAT it was derived from but not WHAT IT DEPENDED ON, and the one field that could have carried that dependency was maintained by memory.

blocks.title: Root cause, one layer under the filed root cause

blocks.text: Direction: provenance over guesswork, and no signal dies unheard

content.value: Three moves on the P0, then the truth-telling repairs around it.

blocks.text: Move 1 - make the renderer version DERIVED, not declared

content.value: Compute the render version as a digest over the renderer's own source or bytecode, so any diff under portable_doc/render changes it automatically. No human bump. No forgotten deploy step. The failure mode that produced this outage becomes unreachable rather than documented.

blocks.text: Move 2 - the reader consults provenance, self-heals drift, and 422s only genuine ambiguity

items.value: Cache stamp differs from the current renderer digest, so the difference IS drift by construction: serve from blocks (canonical) and refresh the cache. No 422.
Cache stamp matches the current digest and bytes still differ, so the HTML was NOT derived from these blocks: that is exactly the ambiguity the 422 exists for. Keep 422.
No stamp at all (legacy): provenance unknown, so drift cannot be claimed. Fail closed on today's behaviour, and shrink this class to zero with a rehydration sweep.

content.value: This deletes the entire false-alarm class while preserving the original safety property exactly, which is the whole point, because the alternative deletes the safety property.

blocks.text: Move 3 - every signal must reach someone

content.value: .github/workflows/paper-readers.yml runs nightly against the live production corpus, and on failure it uploads a JSON artifact and tells nobody. There is no notify step, no issue, no task. That is why it sat RED and UNREAD for three consecutive days. A gate that fails into the void is not a gate. Failure must file a bp task - the repo's own ledger is the alerting channel, and dogfooding it is the honest choice.

blocks.text: The truth-telling repairs around it

items.value: note silent loss - the fix is NOT to make note read content. It is a slot-coverage contract: authoring a block with fields no renderer consumes must not return 200. Prove it at the note block, then census compose.ex's roughly thirty block types for the same shape.

format gate - an always-red advisory signal is worse than no signal, because it trains dismissal of every red beside it. Two honest options: format main once and make it required, or delete the job. The status quo is the only dishonest one.
oauth replay flake - a test that fails on seed order reports a defect that does not exist; it blocked a CSS-only PR.
pr-task-gate - the gate accepts lifecycle_status open plus an active claim; correct builders that close on met criteria contradict it. The gate must encode the doctrine, not fight it.

content.value: The lead tried to prove the cache mechanism by mutating a stored body_html. It measured NOTHING - publish regenerates the cache, so the mutation was silently overwritten and the page stayed 200, appearing to REFUTE a correct hypothesis. Checking STATE (the marker was gone; length unchanged) exposed it. Every fix in this wave ships with a test proven able to fail, asserting STATE rather than an exit code. No republish-based mutation may stand as proof of a cache path.

blocks.title: Surface fence

blocks.text: Direction debate

content.value: Three rivals were developed and argued. The winner is not the option the lead ranked first, and that option loses on the lead's own stated principle.

blocks.text: Rival A - kill the cache

content.value: body_html is derived state, and derived state that can drift is a permanent bug source. Render from blocks on every read; keep body_html only for legacy HTML-only papers that have no blocks. Drift becomes impossible rather than managed. Its strongest argument is uncomfortable: conflicting_html_cache?/4 ALREADY re-renders the full block list on every single read, so the render cost we fear is a cost we are already paying. Rejected for THIS wave because body_html is consumed well beyond the reader - email delivery, SSE delta frames, the source controller, exports - making it a multi-consumer storage migration, not a defect fix. It is a strong candidate for a LATER wave, and provenance is a prerequisite step toward it, not an obstacle.

blocks.text: Rival B - gate the renderer in CI

content.value: Pure CI: any diff under portable_doc/render/ triggers a corpus re-render sweep and an auto-rehydrate on deploy. No runtime change. Rejected as a primary because it protects only THIS repo's deploys - papers published by external producers, or restored from backup, still drift - and it leaves the read path fully capable of 422ing a perfectly renderable paper. It treats the trigger, not the generator. ABSORBED as a secondary slice: belt to provenance's braces.

blocks.text: Rival C - the lead's first preference: prefer blocks whenever blocks are valid

content.value: Tempting, simple, and it does fix the symptom. Rejected because it DELETES a real safety property. A legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list would silently render the thin version: content loss behind HTTP 200. That is the note-block defect at document scale, and it is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate. Rival C converts a loud false alarm into a silent wrong-value generator. Provenance delivers C's entire benefit without C's cost.

Provenance is the only option that removes the false alarms WITHOUT creating a silent loss, requires no storage migration, and leaves kill-the-cache fully open as a later wave. It also uses machinery the repo already built and then forgot to wire in - the cheapest possible bold move.

blocks.title: Why the winner won

blocks.text: The sharpest attack on the winner

content.value: A compile-time renderer digest is only sound if render output depends on the renderer ALONE. It may not. Labels.paper_render_opts/3 threads dataset, style and tenant scope; the label spine performs DB lookups; task_resolver.ex (455 lines) appears to resolve LIVE task state into rendered HTML; StatusVocab and tokens_gen feed the emit. If render output depends on live database state, then rendered != html can differ for reasons that are NEITHER renderer drift NOR block divergence: a referenced task changed status since publish, and the paper 422s. That would mean a whole additional 422 class nobody has seen yet.

If true, it does not kill the direction - it strengthens it. It would prove the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, making provenance the only workable replacement and forcing the digest to cover render INPUTS as well as render code. This is survey question 1, and the verify fleet must settle it before Decide.

The wave therefore needs a synthetic, deterministic harness - write a paper, freeze a cache rendered by a prior renderer, read it - that shows 422 BEFORE the fix and 200 AFTER. Anything less is a vacuous green.

blocks.text: Survey digest - 16 reports folded, 2026-07-20

content.value: Sixteen surveyors returned. The direction survives, but it does NOT survive unchanged: two attacks landed hard enough to add mandatory scope, and one of them inverts the safety argument that justified the winner over Rival C. Everything below is anchored to file:line or to a command a surveyor actually ran; unanchored prose was discarded.

blocks.text: Established - the mechanism, at source

items.value: conflicting_html_cache?/4 (papers.ex:129-138) never reads content[body_html_sv]. Confirmed by grep: zero occurrences of the stamp anywhere in papers.ex. The byte-compare is unconditional. The stamp is write-only - six writers, zero readers on the read path.

The blast radius is exactly 4 call sites of reader_source/3: BulldocsLive mount (raises InvalidSource, plug_status 422 - a HARD page error for fresh loads and crawlers), BulldocsLive refetch (soft in-place degrade), BulldocsSourceController, BulldocsEmailController. Studio is NOT affected - it reads via get_document/get_paper and never calls reader_source. An author can always edit and republish while the public page is dead.

Because all five downstream consumer surfaces (GUI, email, /source, bp paper view, TUI paper pane) merely relay reader_source's return, fixing classification INSIDE papers.ex un-breaks all five with zero edits outside the surface fence.

Corpus, re-counted live today: 419 published papers, not 416. 278 carry sv==3 (all with both blocks and body_html). 141 carry NO stamp: 81 blocks-only (safe - the nil-html guard at papers.ex:129-131 short-circuits before the compare), 49 html-only (no blocks to compare), and 11 with BOTH fields and no stamp - that is the entire real fail-closed class, and all 11 are stale lvd-* demo fixtures from 07-09. Zero papers sit at sv==1 or sv==2.

Today's green is a hand-patched snapshot, not an architectural fix. The 07-18 audit run recorded audited 316 / passed 314 / failed 2. The 07-19 scheduled run failed at the inventory query and never reached the byte-compare at all. render.ex:53 still reads @body_html_render_version 3, unbumped, after four S-tier renderer rounds.

blocks.text: Established - the machinery the fix would use

items.value: A compile-time derived digest is FEASIBLE and has an in-repo precedent to copy nearly verbatim: status_vocab.ex:15-21 already does @external_resource + compile-time File.read! over design/status-manifest.json. Recommended: sha256 over an EXPLICITLY SORTED file list, source text only.

The bytecode alternative was tested, not assumed. :beam_lib.md5/1 is rebuild-stable across build paths and comment-only edits, and does change on a real semantic edit. But raw whole-.beam-file MD5 is NOT stable (it embeds the absolute source path in compile_info) - a naive 'hash the beam' implementation would become a permanent false alarm, exactly the failure it was meant to prevent. beam_lib.md5 also needs siblings compiled and loaded (chicken-and-egg at render.ex's own compile time) and is sensitive to the compiler version, which this repo's ARM/ASDF toolchain split makes a live risk. Source-text hashing sidesteps all of it.

The covered module set, traced through the actual call graph rather than guessed: render.ex + all 16 files under render/ + slots.ex (transitively in the path via components.ex:29 and cards_email.ex:49) = about 10,840 lines. Tiers.ex and Constraints.ex are NOT in the render call graph - the direction's open question on those two resolves to NO.

The reproduction harness needs no discovery. THREE proven bypass seams already exist in the tree: an in-memory %Document{} struct with no Repo call at all (reader_source is pure over a Document - papers_reader_source_test.exs:145-153), Ecto.Changeset.change + Repo.update! (bulldocs_source_controller_test.exs:33-39), and Document.changeset + Repo.update (body_html_render_version_test.exs:184-204). Document.changeset/2 (document.ex:81-105) is a bare cast with zero rendering or stamping. The lead's republish trap is fully avoidable and a builder can copy a recipe rather than search for one.

The alerting seam exists and is proven live: pr-task-gate.yml files a bp task from CI with curl POST /v1/data/mutate/production + createIfNotExists, using repo var BARKPARK_LEDGER_BASE and secret BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN - both already reused by reland-check.yml. Move 3 should reuse this, not invent a fifth mechanism.

blocks.text: THE ATTACK THAT LANDED - the digest is necessary but NOT sufficient

content.value: My sharpest attack aimed at task_resolver and MISSED - TaskResolver is genuinely pure (its moduledoc says 'No DB - inject any fetcher') and resolve_tasks_in_blocks/3 is never called inside the 422 gate; it only runs downstream at display time. But the same attack landed through a different door, and this is the single most important finding of the survey.

Labels.paper_render_opts/3 - the SAME opts-builder used by both the cache-write sites (block_ops.ex:206,210,425-426,552-553) and the 422 gate itself (papers.ex:133-138) - supplies two live closures: ref_resolver and codelist_resolver. reference_title/4 (labels.ex:60-91) runs a live Ecto query against documents. codelist_label/3 leads to Codelists.lookup/3 (codelists.ex:218-237), three Repo reads. Both are invoked inside render_block/2 (render.ex:215-227, 239-252).

Consequence: render_blocks/2 called twice with identical blocks and identical opts can produce different bytes if, in between, someone RENAMES a referenced paper or EDITS a codelist label. Renderer untouched. Blocks untouched. Bytes differ. Under the proposed rule - stamp equals current digest AND bytes differ therefore genuine divergence therefore keep the 422 - this is misclassified and hard-fails a perfectly renderable paper. A third case exists that the two-way drift/divergence split does not name: EXTERNAL REFERENT DRIFT. Prior art corroborates the seam is real and was already the subject of a parity bug (task pbw-w1-reader-resolver-fix, PR #4050, merged 07-18).

This strengthens the direction rather than killing it - it proves the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, which makes Rival C more dangerous and Rival B useless. But it means the P0 slice CANNOT ship as 'derive the digest' alone. Verify V1 settles whether this class bites the live corpus.

blocks.text: THE SECOND ATTACK - the lying stamp, which would make my fix WORSE than the bug

content.value: block_ops.ex:208-232 DELIBERATELY leaves an existing body_html_sv in place when body_html is written verbatim or carried over rather than freshly rendered. The code says so in its own comment at 223-226. writer.ex:492-538 has the mirror shape on the generic mutate path: maybe_sanitize_paper_body_html can rewrite body_html without touching the stamp.

Today this is harmless by accident, because the reader ignores the stamp and the byte-compare still catches the record. But the moment the reader trusts 'stamp not equal to current digest therefore drift therefore serve from blocks and overwrite the cache', a renderer-version bump AFTER such a write converts a genuinely DIVERGENT record into an apparent drift - and the reader silently regenerates from the stale blocks, destroying deliberately-supplied content behind HTTP 200. That is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate, and my winning direction would introduce it. A write-side companion that CLEARS the stamp on any body_html write not derived from the current blocks is therefore MANDATORY scope, not optional polish. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html already has this exposure today, independent of any reader change.

blocks.text: What lowers the stakes - the divergence class is empirically empty

content.value: Every real firing of this gate on record was DRIFT, never divergence: 53 papers caught when the fence first deployed (all 'reconciled through the canonical publish path'), plus the 3 on 07-20, all fixed by clearing body_html and republishing - the drift resolution. If any had been divergence, republishing from blocks would have reported content loss; the epic's own zero-tolerance content-loss counter stayed at zero across 885+ observations. The only test of the divergence branch is a synthetic hand-built fixture. The gate was introduced as adversarial-review hardening (commit 755cff204), not as a fix for an observed incident.

This resolves two things at once. It confirms Rival C's cost is theoretical rather than observed - but 'never seen' is not 'cannot happen', the branch is reachable, and provenance keeps the fail-closed branch for free, so we still keep it. And it lowers the practical severity of the lying stamp (a lying stamp can only lose content on a record that IS divergent, and none are known to exist) while RAISING the relative severity of the resolver-drift class, because that is the one that actually fires.

blocks.text: The rehydration sweep is not a solved prerequisite

items.value: It has never been run in production. Direct evidence: the 07-20 incident's papers were hand-repaired by clear-and-republish rather than by running the sweep it exists to serve. No workflow, deploy script, or ops doc invokes it anywhere in the tree.

It is not paper-scoped and has no status filter - it sweeps EVERY document of any type carrying blocks plus body_html, drafts included, via one unbatched Repo.all with no dry-run and no scoping flags.
Render.render_blocks/2 runs unrescued inside the reduce, so one bad row aborts the whole sweep with no checkpoint - a real risk for a first full-corpus run right after four renderer rounds.
It writes via raw Repo.update, bypassing Content's broadcast layer and any plugin before_save hooks.

Its staleness check is ORDINAL (sv >= current). A hash digest has no ordering, so this must become equality in the same change - and on cutover every existing row reads as non-current, making the sweep's noop fast-path go cold across the entire corpus at once.

blocks.text: Premise corrections - four briefs were wrong, including mine

items.value: 419 published papers today, not 416. The audit's own inventory read 416 two and a half hours earlier; the gap is most likely ordinary corpus growth but was not id-diffed.

Move 3's target list is smaller than assumed. Only THREE workflows carry a schedule: trigger - paper-readers, codebase-intel (drift-guard job) and renew-mail-cert. aesthetics-guard, astro-finder-drift, deploy-harnesses and security are push/PR-only and out of scope for 'nightly gate goes red'. Separately: renew-mail-cert has ZERO failure handling of any kind, which means a failed monthly TLS renewal has about 90 days of silent runway.

The oauth flake pointers were wrong. oauth_test.exs:77/85 (verify_state) touch only the sandboxed oauth_states table and are immune - a surveyor PROVED this by racing a config mutation against a live verify_state call and getting :ok. The real flake is router_oauth_test.exs, caused by oauth_test.exs:33-44 doing a NODE-GLOBAL Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, blank-creds) under async:true while another async module calls fetch_identity, which reads that config at call time and returns :provider_not_enabled. Reproduced causally: error during the window, ok after restore.

The pr-task-gate rule is NOT in the yml near line 104 (that is the hotfix lane's task-creation literal). It is scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91-92. It also compounds with a lease-lapse deadlock: claim.ex:26 restricts claiming to open|blocked, so an in_progress task whose lease expired is UNCLAIMABLE - the gate demands a recovery action the ledger's own API structurally refuses. Both are already filed; this cycle diagnoses only, since every file involved sits outside the surface fence.

content.value: Ten assignments. This round does not browse; it closes the unknowns Decide cannot proceed without. Models are chosen so that Opus carries anything where being wrong is expensive.

blocks.text: Verification results - what the deep round proved, and where it overturned the plan

content.value: Ten verifiers flew. Three of them contradicted the strategic direction, and in every case the evidence won. What follows quotes the decisive proof lines rather than summarising them.

blocks.text: PROVEN: the mechanism, and that provenance is unread

content.value: conflicting_html_cache?/4 (papers.ex:129-138) byte-compares a fresh render against the stored HTML and never reads content[body_html_sv] - grep returns zero occurrences of the stamp anywhere in papers.ex. Six writers, zero readers. Stronger than the grep, a behavioural sweep over sv values [absent, nil, 1, 2, 3, 99] proved all six produce the IDENTICAL 422: 'provenance is NOT consulted: sv=1 and sv=current both give {:error, :ambiguous_source}'. Provenance cannot influence the verdict, rather than merely being absent from the file.

The blast radius is exactly 4 reader_source/3 call sites, all public-reader; Studio is untouched because it reads via get_document/get_paper. A fix inside papers.ex un-breaks five downstream surfaces with zero edits outside the fence.

blocks.text: PROVEN: the digest mechanism, and that the obvious implementation would have been wrong

content.value: Two independent builds of identical source gave a byte-identical digest: df438146989a86763ef4c9fd97d022e409fb884e69d7432a424f458e1cb46d24 both times. Appending one byte to render/walk.ex moved it to 58bcc60a8be39e05e4833e02df68f91c3cbede3299821b684f3d0e568eaf5eeb; reverting restored the original exactly.

A surveyor TESTED the alternative rather than assuming it. :beam_lib.md5/1 is rebuild-stable, but raw whole-.beam MD5 is NOT - it embeds the absolute source path (35E919CE... vs A4AA7823... for two path-only-different builds). A naive 'hash the beam' implementation would have become the permanent false alarm it was meant to prevent.

blocks.title: The near miss

content.value: The covered set was settled by an Erlang trace, not by reading: trace_pattern on Tiers and Constraints while running render_blocks/2 over callout/note/stage/card captured 'Tiers/Constraints calls during render_blocks/2: []'. Both modules stay out. slots.ex stays in.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (1): the byte-compare has a THIRD failure class nobody named

content.value: My own sharpest attack aimed at task_resolver and MISSED - TaskResolver is genuinely pure and resolve_tasks_in_blocks is never called inside the 422 gate. The identical attack then landed through a different door.

Labels.paper_render_opts/3 - the SAME opts builder used by both the cache-write sites and the 422 gate - supplies ref_resolver and codelist_resolver closures that run live Ecto queries. A probe created a referent, authored a field-reference block at it, wrote a byte-exact body_html, stamped the CURRENT version, and confirmed {:blocks, _}. The ONLY subsequent mutation was renaming the REFERENT. reader_source then returned {:error, :ambiguous_source}. Same for a codelist relabel. Mutation-proof on both: 'left: {:blocks, _} / right: {:error, :ambiguous_source}'.

Under the proposed rule - stamp == digest AND bytes differ implies divergence, keep the 422 - that paper is MISCLASSIFIED and hard-fails. This is EXTERNAL REFERENT DRIFT, and neither 'drift' nor 'divergence' covers it. It strengthens the direction rather than killing it: it proves the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, which makes Rival C more dangerous and Rival B useless. But the P0 could not ship as 'derive the digest' alone.

Sized: exactly 1 of 419 published papers carries either block type (portabledoc-showcase), and it is ARMED - sv=3, a 53,077-byte cache with the live-resolved title 'Diagrams that draw themselves in the terminal' baked in, whose referent is itself a published paper. N=1 is a snapshot, not a bound.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (2): the write path deliberately preserves a lying stamp, and the digest ARMS it

content.value: block_ops.ex:208-232 preserves an existing body_html_sv on verbatim body_html writes; its own comment at :223-226 says this is deliberate. Harmless today only because the reader ignores the stamp. A probe drove the real upsert path and produced a persisted record classified three ways:

items.value: TODAY -> {:error, :ambiguous_source} - 422, safe
RULE @ v3 (stamp == current) -> :divergence_keep_422 - 422, safe
RULE @ v4 (stamp != current) -> :drift_serve_blocks_and_overwrite - 200, and 'CONTENT LOSS: 52 bytes discarded behind HTTP 200'

content.value: Nothing about the record changes between rows 2 and 3. The only mover is the renderer version - which the digest slice makes move on EVERY renderer commit. Move 1 and Move 2 are individually sound and jointly load a gun. The write-side stamp clear became mandatory co-scope, not polish.

blocks.title: Why two correct fixes are dangerous together

content.value: The remedy is Map.delete, not a sentinel: a sentinel is by construction != current, so it routes straight into the overwrite branch - fail-open by discipline. Control proved Map.delete holds: ':unknown_fail_closed' at BOTH v3 and v4. And it must key on is_binary(attrs[body_html]), NOT on not is_list(blocks) - the pure carry-over leg produces a fully coherent record (reader => :blocks), so a blanket delete would manufacture new false 422s.

A hazard nobody had flagged also surfaced: the writer persists a CALLER-SUPPLIED stamp verbatim ('[no-blocks attrs] persisted sv = 1'). Under the new rule that is a client-controlled classification switch.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (3): the validation seam the plan named is dead for 416 of 419 papers

content.value: Constraints.validate/2 IS live and blocking - an injected error returned 409 halted, fail-closed. But Template.validate/1 wraps the whole thing in 'if Enum.any?(blocks, &locked?/1)', and its own docstring says 'Papers with no locked blocks pass untouched'. Live census: 3 papers carry a locked block, 416 do not, and of the papers containing note or card blocks, ZERO are locked. Proven end-to-end: the identical injected error rejects a publish on a locked paper and returns HTTP 200 on an unlocked one.

The patch path is dead through a second door - its before-valid guard only vetoes when the doc was already valid, which legacy papers never are. The seam to use is block_ops' unconditional with-chain beside reject_hollow_result.

The rule shape was measured, not argued: across all 419 papers the NARROW rule flags 5 blocks with ZERO false alarms (all verified genuine by rendering); a positive allowlist flags 38, ~33 of them legal chrome. And 9 slot-shaped blocks across 6 published papers are silently dropping prose right now - this is not hypothetical.

blocks.text: The finding under the finding

content.value: The lead's mechanism is correct and I verified it at source. Content.Papers.reader_source/3 (api/lib/barkpark/content/papers.ex:60-138) classifies a paper's canonical blocks, and conflicting_html_cache?/4 re-renders those blocks with the CURRENT renderer and compares bytes against the stored body_html cache. Any difference becomes {:error, :ambiguous_source} and then HTTP 422. A renderer change therefore kills every unedited published paper that uses a touched block type.
But the byte-compare is doing DOUBLE DUTY, and that conflation is the real defect. It cannot tell apart two completely different situations:

items.value: DRIFT - the cache was rendered from THESE blocks by an OLDER renderer. Harmless. Self-healable. The blocks are canonical and re-rendering them is strictly safe.

DIVERGENCE - the stored HTML carries content the blocks do not (a legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list). Genuinely ambiguous. Preferring blocks here would silently destroy content.

content.value: The 422 was built for case 2. It fires on case 1 because a byte-compare has no way to ask which one it is looking at.

content[body_html_sv] is a render-version stamp written by SIX write sites (block_ops.ex:1313, writer.ex:529, sheets.ex:151, proposals.ex:151, doctrine_backfill.ex:493, composition_migration.ex:686). Render.body_html_render_version/0 declares it. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html re-renders any cache whose stamp lags. reader_source/3 never reads the stamp. It byte-compares instead.

blocks.title: The machinery to tell them apart already exists, and the read path ignores it

content.value: And the stamp itself is a hand-typed integer. api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render.ex:53 holds @body_html_render_version 3 above a comment instructing a human to bump it when render semantics change, and a second comment describing a manual deploy step: run mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html on guerrilla and prod after this wave merges. Four S-tier pdrender rounds landed on 07-18 (#4126, #4140, #4192) and a status-manifest change on 07-19 (#4394). Nobody bumped it. Nobody ran the sweep.

A version a human must remember to bump is not a version - it is a wish. The cache recorded WHAT it was derived from but not WHAT IT DEPENDED ON, and the one field that could have carried that dependency was maintained by memory.

blocks.title: Root cause, one layer under the filed root cause

blocks.text: Direction: provenance over guesswork, and no signal dies unheard

content.value: Three moves on the P0, then the truth-telling repairs around it.

blocks.text: Move 1 - make the renderer version DERIVED, not declared

content.value: Compute the render version as a digest over the renderer's own source or bytecode, so any diff under portable_doc/render changes it automatically. No human bump. No forgotten deploy step. The failure mode that produced this outage becomes unreachable rather than documented.

blocks.text: Move 2 - the reader consults provenance, self-heals drift, and 422s only genuine ambiguity

items.value: Cache stamp differs from the current renderer digest, so the difference IS drift by construction: serve from blocks (canonical) and refresh the cache. No 422.
Cache stamp matches the current digest and bytes still differ, so the HTML was NOT derived from these blocks: that is exactly the ambiguity the 422 exists for. Keep 422.
No stamp at all (legacy): provenance unknown, so drift cannot be claimed. Fail closed on today's behaviour, and shrink this class to zero with a rehydration sweep.

content.value: This deletes the entire false-alarm class while preserving the original safety property exactly, which is the whole point, because the alternative deletes the safety property.

blocks.text: Move 3 - every signal must reach someone

content.value: .github/workflows/paper-readers.yml runs nightly against the live production corpus, and on failure it uploads a JSON artifact and tells nobody. There is no notify step, no issue, no task. That is why it sat RED and UNREAD for three consecutive days. A gate that fails into the void is not a gate. Failure must file a bp task - the repo's own ledger is the alerting channel, and dogfooding it is the honest choice.

blocks.text: The truth-telling repairs around it

items.value: note silent loss - the fix is NOT to make note read content. It is a slot-coverage contract: authoring a block with fields no renderer consumes must not return 200. Prove it at the note block, then census compose.ex's roughly thirty block types for the same shape.

format gate - an always-red advisory signal is worse than no signal, because it trains dismissal of every red beside it. Two honest options: format main once and make it required, or delete the job. The status quo is the only dishonest one.

pr-task-gate - the gate accepts lifecycle_status open plus an active claim; correct builders that close on met criteria contradict it. The gate must encode the doctrine, not fight it.

blocks.title: Surface fence

blocks.text: Direction debate

content.value: Three rivals were developed and argued. The winner is not the option the lead ranked first, and that option loses on the lead's own stated principle.

blocks.text: Rival A - kill the cache

content.value: body_html is derived state, and derived state that can drift is a permanent bug source. Render from blocks on every read; keep body_html only for legacy HTML-only papers that have no blocks. Drift becomes impossible rather than managed. Its strongest argument is uncomfortable: conflicting_html_cache?/4 ALREADY re-renders the full block list on every single read, so the render cost we fear is a cost we are already paying. Rejected for THIS wave because body_html is consumed well beyond the reader - email delivery, SSE delta frames, the source controller, exports - making it a multi-consumer storage migration, not a defect fix. It is a strong candidate for a LATER wave, and provenance is a prerequisite step toward it, not an obstacle.

blocks.text: Rival B - gate the renderer in CI

content.value: Pure CI: any diff under portable_doc/render/ triggers a corpus re-render sweep and an auto-rehydrate on deploy. No runtime change. Rejected as a primary because it protects only THIS repo's deploys - papers published by external producers, or restored from backup, still drift - and it leaves the read path fully capable of 422ing a perfectly renderable paper. It treats the trigger, not the generator. ABSORBED as a secondary slice: belt to provenance's braces.

blocks.text: Rival C - the lead's first preference: prefer blocks whenever blocks are valid

content.value: Tempting, simple, and it does fix the symptom. Rejected because it DELETES a real safety property. A legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list would silently render the thin version: content loss behind HTTP 200. That is the note-block defect at document scale, and it is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate. Rival C converts a loud false alarm into a silent wrong-value generator. Provenance delivers C's entire benefit without C's cost.

Provenance is the only option that removes the false alarms WITHOUT creating a silent loss, requires no storage migration, and leaves kill-the-cache fully open as a later wave. It also uses machinery the repo already built and then forgot to wire in - the cheapest possible bold move.

blocks.title: Why the winner won

blocks.text: The sharpest attack on the winner

content.value: A compile-time renderer digest is only sound if render output depends on the renderer ALONE. It may not. Labels.paper_render_opts/3 threads dataset, style and tenant scope; the label spine performs DB lookups; task_resolver.ex (455 lines) appears to resolve LIVE task state into rendered HTML; StatusVocab and tokens_gen feed the emit. If render output depends on live database state, then rendered != html can differ for reasons that are NEITHER renderer drift NOR block divergence: a referenced task changed status since publish, and the paper 422s. That would mean a whole additional 422 class nobody has seen yet.

If true, it does not kill the direction - it strengthens it. It would prove the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, making provenance the only workable replacement and forcing the digest to cover render INPUTS as well as render code. This is survey question 1, and the verify fleet must settle it before Decide.

blocks.text: Established - the mechanism, at source

items.value: conflicting_html_cache?/4 (papers.ex:129-138) never reads content[body_html_sv]. Confirmed by grep: zero occurrences of the stamp anywhere in papers.ex. The byte-compare is unconditional. The stamp is write-only - six writers, zero readers on the read path.

The blast radius is exactly 4 call sites of reader_source/3: BulldocsLive mount (raises InvalidSource, plug_status 422 - a HARD page error for fresh loads and crawlers), BulldocsLive refetch (soft in-place degrade), BulldocsSourceController, BulldocsEmailController. Studio is NOT affected - it reads via get_document/get_paper and never calls reader_source. An author can always edit and republish while the public page is dead.

Because all five downstream consumer surfaces (GUI, email, /source, bp paper view, TUI paper pane) merely relay reader_source's return, fixing classification INSIDE papers.ex un-breaks all five with zero edits outside the surface fence.

Corpus, re-counted live today: 419 published papers, not 416. 278 carry sv==3 (all with both blocks and body_html). 141 carry NO stamp: 81 blocks-only (safe - the nil-html guard at papers.ex:129-131 short-circuits before the compare), 49 html-only (no blocks to compare), and 11 with BOTH fields and no stamp - that is the entire real fail-closed class, and all 11 are stale lvd-* demo fixtures from 07-09. Zero papers sit at sv==1 or sv==2.

Today's green is a hand-patched snapshot, not an architectural fix. The 07-18 audit run recorded audited 316 / passed 314 / failed 2. The 07-19 scheduled run failed at the inventory query and never reached the byte-compare at all. render.ex:53 still reads @body_html_render_version 3, unbumped, after four S-tier renderer rounds.

blocks.text: Established - the machinery the fix would use

items.value: A compile-time derived digest is FEASIBLE and has an in-repo precedent to copy nearly verbatim: status_vocab.ex:15-21 already does @external_resource + compile-time File.read! over design/status-manifest.json. Recommended: sha256 over an EXPLICITLY SORTED file list, source text only.

The bytecode alternative was tested, not assumed. :beam_lib.md5/1 is rebuild-stable across build paths and comment-only edits, and does change on a real semantic edit. But raw whole-.beam-file MD5 is NOT stable (it embeds the absolute source path in compile_info) - a naive 'hash the beam' implementation would become a permanent false alarm, exactly the failure it was meant to prevent. beam_lib.md5 also needs siblings compiled and loaded (chicken-and-egg at render.ex's own compile time) and is sensitive to the compiler version, which this repo's ARM/ASDF toolchain split makes a live risk. Source-text hashing sidesteps all of it.

The covered module set, traced through the actual call graph rather than guessed: render.ex + all 16 files under render/ + slots.ex (transitively in the path via components.ex:29 and cards_email.ex:49) = about 10,840 lines. Tiers.ex and Constraints.ex are NOT in the render call graph - the direction's open question on those two resolves to NO.

The reproduction harness needs no discovery. THREE proven bypass seams already exist in the tree: an in-memory %Document{} struct with no Repo call at all (reader_source is pure over a Document - papers_reader_source_test.exs:145-153), Ecto.Changeset.change + Repo.update! (bulldocs_source_controller_test.exs:33-39), and Document.changeset + Repo.update (body_html_render_version_test.exs:184-204). Document.changeset/2 (document.ex:81-105) is a bare cast with zero rendering or stamping. The lead's republish trap is fully avoidable and a builder can copy a recipe rather than search for one.

The alerting seam exists and is proven live: pr-task-gate.yml files a bp task from CI with curl POST /v1/data/mutate/production + createIfNotExists, using repo var BARKPARK_LEDGER_BASE and secret BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN - both already reused by reland-check.yml. blocks.text: THE ATTACK THAT LANDED - the digest is necessary but NOT sufficient

content.value: My sharpest attack aimed at task_resolver and MISSED - TaskResolver is genuinely pure (its moduledoc says 'No DB - inject any fetcher') and resolve_tasks_in_blocks/3 is never called inside the 422 gate; it only runs downstream at display time. But the same attack landed through a different door, and this is the single most important finding of the survey.

Labels.paper_render_opts/3 - the SAME opts-builder used by both the cache-write sites (block_ops.ex:206,210,425-426,552-553) and the 422 gate itself (papers.ex:133-138) - supplies two live closures: ref_resolver and codelist_resolver. reference_title/4 (labels.ex:60-91) runs a live Ecto query against documents. codelist_label/3 leads to Codelists.lookup/3 (codelists.ex:218-237), three Repo reads. Both are invoked inside render_block/2 (render.ex:215-227, 239-252).

Consequence: render_blocks/2 called twice with identical blocks and identical opts can produce different bytes if, in between, someone RENAMES a referenced paper or EDITS a codelist label. Renderer untouched. Blocks untouched. Bytes differ. Under the proposed rule - stamp equals current digest AND bytes differ therefore genuine divergence therefore keep the 422 - this is misclassified and hard-fails a perfectly renderable paper. A third case exists that the two-way drift/divergence split does not name: EXTERNAL REFERENT DRIFT. Prior art corroborates the seam is real and was already the subject of a parity bug (task pbw-w1-reader-resolver-fix, PR #4050, merged 07-18).

This strengthens the direction rather than killing it - it proves the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, which makes Rival C more dangerous and Rival B useless. But it means the P0 slice CANNOT ship as 'derive the digest' alone. Verify V1 settles whether this class bites the live corpus.

blocks.text: THE SECOND ATTACK - the lying stamp, which would make my fix WORSE than the bug

content.value: block_ops.ex:208-232 DELIBERATELY leaves an existing body_html_sv in place when body_html is written verbatim or carried over rather than freshly rendered. The code says so in its own comment at 223-226. writer.ex:492-538 has the mirror shape on the generic mutate path: maybe_sanitize_paper_body_html can rewrite body_html without touching the stamp.

Today this is harmless by accident, because the reader ignores the stamp and the byte-compare still catches the record. But the moment the reader trusts 'stamp not equal to current digest therefore drift therefore serve from blocks and overwrite the cache', a renderer-version bump AFTER such a write converts a genuinely DIVERGENT record into an apparent drift - and the reader silently regenerates from the stale blocks, destroying deliberately-supplied content behind HTTP 200. That is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate, and my winning direction would introduce it. A write-side companion that CLEARS the stamp on any body_html write not derived from the current blocks is therefore MANDATORY scope, not optional polish. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html already has this exposure today, independent of any reader change.

blocks.text: What lowers the stakes - the divergence class is empirically empty

content.value: Every real firing of this gate on record was DRIFT, never divergence: 53 papers caught when the fence first deployed (all 'reconciled through the canonical publish path'), plus the 3 on 07-20, all fixed by clearing body_html and republishing - the drift resolution. If any had been divergence, republishing from blocks would have reported content loss; the epic's own zero-tolerance content-loss counter stayed at zero across 885+ observations. The only test of the divergence branch is a synthetic hand-built fixture. The gate was introduced as adversarial-review hardening (commit 755cff204), not as a fix for an observed incident.

This resolves two things at once. It confirms Rival C's cost is theoretical rather than observed - but 'never seen' is not 'cannot happen', the branch is reachable, and provenance keeps the fail-closed branch for free, so we still keep it. And it lowers the practical severity of the lying stamp (a lying stamp can only lose content on a record that IS divergent, and none are known to exist) while RAISING the relative severity of the resolver-drift class, because that is the one that actually fires.

blocks.text: The rehydration sweep is not a solved prerequisite

items.value: It has never been run in production. Direct evidence: the 07-20 incident's papers were hand-repaired by clear-and-republish rather than by running the sweep it exists to serve. No workflow, deploy script, or ops doc invokes it anywhere in the tree.

It is not paper-scoped and has no status filter - it sweeps EVERY document of any type carrying blocks plus body_html, drafts included, via one unbatched Repo.all with no dry-run and no scoping flags.
Render.render_blocks/2 runs unrescued inside the reduce, so one bad row aborts the whole sweep with no checkpoint - a real risk for a first full-corpus run right after four renderer rounds.
It writes via raw Repo.update, bypassing Content's broadcast layer and any plugin before_save hooks.

Its staleness check is ORDINAL (sv >= current). A hash digest has no ordering, so this must become equality in the same change - and on cutover every existing row reads as non-current, making the sweep's noop fast-path go cold across the entire corpus at once.

content.value: Ten verifiers flew. Three of them contradicted the strategic direction, and in every case the evidence won. What follows quotes the decisive proof lines rather than summarising them.

blocks.text: PROVEN: the mechanism, and that provenance is unread

content.value: conflicting_html_cache?/4 (papers.ex:129-138) byte-compares a fresh render against the stored HTML and never reads content[body_html_sv] - grep returns zero occurrences of the stamp anywhere in papers.ex. Six writers, zero readers. Stronger than the grep, a behavioural sweep over sv values [absent, nil, 1, 2, 3, 99] proved all six produce the IDENTICAL 422: 'provenance is NOT consulted: sv=1 and sv=current both give {:error, :ambiguous_source}'. Provenance cannot influence the verdict, rather than merely being absent from the file.

The blast radius is exactly 4 reader_source/3 call sites, all public-reader; Studio is untouched because it reads via get_document/get_paper. A fix inside papers.ex un-breaks five downstream surfaces with zero edits outside the fence.

blocks.text: PROVEN: the digest mechanism, and that the obvious implementation would have been wrong

content.value: Two independent builds of identical source gave a byte-identical digest: df438146989a86763ef4c9fd97d022e409fb884e69d7432a424f458e1cb46d24 both times. Appending one byte to render/walk.ex moved it to 58bcc60a8be39e05e4833e02df68f91c3cbede3299821b684f3d0e568eaf5eeb; reverting restored the original exactly.

A surveyor TESTED the alternative rather than assuming it. :beam_lib.md5/1 is rebuild-stable, but raw whole-.beam MD5 is NOT - it embeds the absolute source path (35E919CE... vs A4AA7823... for two path-only-different builds). A naive 'hash the beam' implementation would have become the permanent false alarm it was meant to prevent.

blocks.title: The near miss

content.value: The covered set was settled by an Erlang trace, not by reading: trace_pattern on Tiers and Constraints while running render_blocks/2 over callout/note/stage/card captured 'Tiers/Constraints calls during render_blocks/2: []'. Both modules stay out. slots.ex stays in.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (1): the byte-compare has a THIRD failure class nobody named

content.value: My own sharpest attack aimed at task_resolver and MISSED - TaskResolver is genuinely pure and resolve_tasks_in_blocks is never called inside the 422 gate. The identical attack then landed through a different door.

Labels.paper_render_opts/3 - the SAME opts builder used by both the cache-write sites and the 422 gate - supplies ref_resolver and codelist_resolver closures that run live Ecto queries. A probe created a referent, authored a field-reference block at it, wrote a byte-exact body_html, stamped the CURRENT version, and confirmed {:blocks, _}. The ONLY subsequent mutation was renaming the REFERENT. reader_source then returned {:error, :ambiguous_source}. Same for a codelist relabel. Mutation-proof on both: 'left: {:blocks, _} / right: {:error, :ambiguous_source}'.

Under the proposed rule - stamp == digest AND bytes differ implies divergence, keep the 422 - that paper is MISCLASSIFIED and hard-fails. This is EXTERNAL REFERENT DRIFT, and neither 'drift' nor 'divergence' covers it. It strengthens the direction rather than killing it: it proves the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, which makes Rival C more dangerous and Rival B useless. But the P0 could not ship as 'derive the digest' alone.

Sized: exactly 1 of 419 published papers carries either block type (portabledoc-showcase), and it is ARMED - sv=3, a 53,077-byte cache with the live-resolved title 'Diagrams that draw themselves in the terminal' baked in, whose referent is itself a published paper. N=1 is a snapshot, not a bound.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (2): the write path deliberately preserves a lying stamp, and the digest ARMS it

content.value: block_ops.ex:208-232 preserves an existing body_html_sv on verbatim body_html writes; its own comment at :223-226 says this is deliberate. Harmless today only because the reader ignores the stamp. A probe drove the real upsert path and produced a persisted record classified three ways:

items.value: TODAY -> {:error, :ambiguous_source} - 422, safe
RULE @ v3 (stamp == current) -> :divergence_keep_422 - 422, safe
RULE @ v4 (stamp != current) -> :drift_serve_blocks_and_overwrite - 200, and 'CONTENT LOSS: 52 bytes discarded behind HTTP 200'

content.value: Nothing about the record changes between rows 2 and 3. The only mover is the renderer version - which the digest slice makes move on EVERY renderer commit. Move 1 and Move 2 are individually sound and jointly load a gun. The write-side stamp clear became mandatory co-scope, not polish.

blocks.title: Why two correct fixes are dangerous together

content.value: The remedy is Map.delete, not a sentinel: a sentinel is by construction != current, so it routes straight into the overwrite branch - fail-open by discipline. Control proved Map.delete holds: ':unknown_fail_closed' at BOTH v3 and v4. And it must key on is_binary(attrs[body_html]), NOT on not is_list(blocks) - the pure carry-over leg produces a fully coherent record (reader => :blocks), so a blanket delete would manufacture new false 422s.

A hazard nobody had flagged also surfaced: the writer persists a CALLER-SUPPLIED stamp verbatim ('[no-blocks attrs] persisted sv = 1'). Under the new rule that is a client-controlled classification switch.

blocks.text: OVERTURNED (3): the validation seam the plan named is dead for 416 of 419 papers

content.value: Constraints.validate/2 IS live and blocking - an injected error returned 409 halted, fail-closed. But Template.validate/1 wraps the whole thing in 'if Enum.any?(blocks, &locked?/1)', and its own docstring says 'Papers with no locked blocks pass untouched'. Live census: 3 papers carry a locked block, 416 do not, and of the papers containing note or card blocks, ZERO are locked. Proven end-to-end: the identical injected error rejects a publish on a locked paper and returns HTTP 200 on an unlocked one.

The patch path is dead through a second door - its before-valid guard only vetoes when the doc was already valid, which legacy papers never are. The seam to use is block_ops' unconditional with-chain beside reject_hollow_result.

The rule shape was measured, not argued: across all 419 papers the NARROW rule flags 5 blocks with ZERO false alarms (all verified genuine by rendering); a positive allowlist flags 38, ~33 of them legal chrome. And 9 slot-shaped blocks across 6 published papers are silently dropping prose right now - this is not hypothetical.

blocks.text: PROVEN: the alerting remedy would itself have been a wrong-value generator

content.value: BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN does not exist in ANY scope - 5 repo secrets, none of them it; all 6 deployment environments empty; org secrets structurally impossible because FRIKKern is a user account (orgs/FRIKKern/actions/secrets 404s). Three workflows already reference it and have been silently degrading since they were written.

Even WITH a token, the shape we would have copied files an invisible task. The exact createIfNotExists body was run against production: HTTP 200, and the response is '"_id":"drafts.probe-ci-filing-DELETEME","_draft":true'. It creates a DRAFT, absent from the published ledger that bp task ready reads - while the workflow prints 'Filed override task'. Copying it would have shipped a nightly alert that files nothing and says it worked.

blocks.text: Decisions

content.value: The full set with reasons is the epic's memory at .claude/workflows/bp-production-truth-charter.md (D1-D31), committed. This Paper carries the wave's story; the charter carries the epic's. They must not fork. The load-bearing ones:

D8 - stamp != digest is drift (serve blocks); stamp == digest with differing bytes is divergence (keep the 422); no stamp fails closed: removes the false-alarm class while preserving the safety property exactly.
D9 - resolver-dependent blocks are exempt from the byte-compare: their bytes are a function of external state the blocks never claimed to pin, so they cannot evidence divergence in either direction.
D10 - do NOT freeze resolved labels: a frozen label makes 'stamp matches' true while the correct rendering legitimately differs, serving the OLD title.
D12/D13/D14 - clear the stamp on the verbatim leg only, via Map.delete and never a sentinel: absent is already fail-closed; a sentinel is fail-open by construction.
D16/D17 - the sweep compares by equality and SKIPS the divergent class: otherwise the stamp clear trades a read-path loss for a sweep-path loss.
D19 - alert via the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, not a bp task: the task token does not exist and the mutation shape files a draft while reporting success.
D22/D23/D24 - narrow rule, blocking write-side ratchet, wired into the unconditional seam: 0 false alarms vs ~33, and the named seam is skipped by 416 of 419 papers.
D27 - the fence is extended to the three scheduled workflows, two scripts and the rehydrate mix task: the fence exists to avoid the Studio and PDS epics, and none of these belong to either.

Epic wave - production truth - 2026-07-20

Stop the surfaces that lie

Five live, user-facing defects filed 2026-07-20. Every one is a wrong-value generator: a surface that reports one thing while the truth is otherwise. This wave pays them, and names the one structural cause that produced the worst of them.

The wish, verbatim

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): Fable 5 is spend-limited - every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'. - THIS CYCLE: pay the PRODUCTION TRUTH defects filed 2026-07-20. These are live, user-facing, and every one of them is a WRONG-VALUE GENERATOR - a surface that reports success while the truth is otherwise. Root task: paper-cache-drift-mass-422-on-renderer-change (priority 0).

The roster

P0paper-cache-drift-mass-422-on-renderer-change. Any PortableDoc renderer change silently 422s every published paper using a touched block type.
P1pd-note-block-silent-content-loss. A note authored with content instead of label/lead/text renders an empty shell behind HTTP 200.
P1cloud-oauth-replay-test-is-seed-flaky. Confirmed flake; blocked a CSS-only PR.
P1pr-task-gate-contradicts-close-on-criteria. The gate demands in_progress while correct builders close on met criteria.
P2format-gate-red-on-main-teaches-dismissal. 91 unformatted files keep an advisory gate permanently red.

The finding under the finding

The lead's mechanism is correct and I verified it at source. Content.Papers.reader_source/3 (api/lib/barkpark/content/papers.ex:60-138) classifies a paper's canonical blocks, and conflicting_html_cache?/4 re-renders those blocks with the CURRENT renderer and compares bytes against the stored body_html cache. Any difference becomes {:error, :ambiguous_source} and then HTTP 422. A renderer change therefore kills every unedited published paper that uses a touched block type.

But the byte-compare is doing DOUBLE DUTY, and that conflation is the real defect. It cannot tell apart two completely different situations:

  • DRIFT - the cache was rendered from THESE blocks by an OLDER renderer. Harmless. Self-healable. The blocks are canonical and re-rendering them is strictly safe.
  • DIVERGENCE - the stored HTML carries content the blocks do not (a legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list). Genuinely ambiguous. Preferring blocks here would silently destroy content.

The 422 was built for case 2. It fires on case 1 because a byte-compare has no way to ask which one it is looking at.

The machinery to tell them apart already exists, and the read path ignores it
content[body_html_sv] is a render-version stamp written by SIX write sites (block_ops.ex:1313, writer.ex:529, sheets.ex:151, proposals.ex:151, doctrine_backfill.ex:493, composition_migration.ex:686). Render.body_html_render_version/0 declares it. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html re-renders any cache whose stamp lags. reader_source/3 never reads the stamp. It byte-compares instead.

And the stamp itself is a hand-typed integer. api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render.ex:53 holds @body_html_render_version 3 above a comment instructing a human to bump it when render semantics change, and a second comment describing a manual deploy step: run mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html on guerrilla and prod after this wave merges. Four S-tier pdrender rounds landed on 07-18 (#4126, #4140, #4192) and a status-manifest change on 07-19 (#4394). Nobody bumped it. Nobody ran the sweep.

Root cause, one layer under the filed root cause
A version a human must remember to bump is not a version - it is a wish. The cache recorded WHAT it was derived from but not WHAT IT DEPENDED ON, and the one field that could have carried that dependency was maintained by memory.

Direction: provenance over guesswork, and no signal dies unheard

Three moves on the P0, then the truth-telling repairs around it.

Move 1 - make the renderer version DERIVED, not declared

Compute the render version as a digest over the renderer's own source or bytecode, so any diff under portable_doc/render changes it automatically. No human bump. No forgotten deploy step. The failure mode that produced this outage becomes unreachable rather than documented.

Move 2 - the reader consults provenance, self-heals drift, and 422s only genuine ambiguity

  • Cache stamp differs from the current renderer digest, so the difference IS drift by construction: serve from blocks (canonical) and refresh the cache. No 422.
  • Cache stamp matches the current digest and bytes still differ, so the HTML was NOT derived from these blocks: that is exactly the ambiguity the 422 exists for. Keep 422.
  • No stamp at all (legacy): provenance unknown, so drift cannot be claimed. Fail closed on today's behaviour, and shrink this class to zero with a rehydration sweep.

This deletes the entire false-alarm class while preserving the original safety property exactly, which is the whole point, because the alternative deletes the safety property.

Move 3 - every signal must reach someone

.github/workflows/paper-readers.yml runs nightly against the live production corpus, and on failure it uploads a JSON artifact and tells nobody. There is no notify step, no issue, no task. That is why it sat RED and UNREAD for three consecutive days. A gate that fails into the void is not a gate. Failure must file a bp task - the repo's own ledger is the alerting channel, and dogfooding it is the honest choice.

The truth-telling repairs around it

  • note silent loss - the fix is NOT to make note read content. It is a slot-coverage contract: authoring a block with fields no renderer consumes must not return 200. Prove it at the note block, then census compose.ex's roughly thirty block types for the same shape.
  • format gate - an always-red advisory signal is worse than no signal, because it trains dismissal of every red beside it. Two honest options: format main once and make it required, or delete the job. The status quo is the only dishonest one.
  • oauth replay flake - a test that fails on seed order reports a defect that does not exist; it blocked a CSS-only PR.
  • pr-task-gate - the gate accepts lifecycle_status open plus an active claim; correct builders that close on met criteria contradict it. The gate must encode the doctrine, not fight it.

Direction debate

Three rivals were developed and argued. The winner is not the option the lead ranked first, and that option loses on the lead's own stated principle.

Rival A - kill the cache

body_html is derived state, and derived state that can drift is a permanent bug source. Render from blocks on every read; keep body_html only for legacy HTML-only papers that have no blocks. Drift becomes impossible rather than managed. Its strongest argument is uncomfortable: conflicting_html_cache?/4 ALREADY re-renders the full block list on every single read, so the render cost we fear is a cost we are already paying. Rejected for THIS wave because body_html is consumed well beyond the reader - email delivery, SSE delta frames, the source controller, exports - making it a multi-consumer storage migration, not a defect fix. It is a strong candidate for a LATER wave, and provenance is a prerequisite step toward it, not an obstacle.

Rival B - gate the renderer in CI

Pure CI: any diff under portable_doc/render/ triggers a corpus re-render sweep and an auto-rehydrate on deploy. No runtime change. Rejected as a primary because it protects only THIS repo's deploys - papers published by external producers, or restored from backup, still drift - and it leaves the read path fully capable of 422ing a perfectly renderable paper. It treats the trigger, not the generator. ABSORBED as a secondary slice: belt to provenance's braces.

Rival C - the lead's first preference: prefer blocks whenever blocks are valid

Tempting, simple, and it does fix the symptom. Rejected because it DELETES a real safety property. A legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list would silently render the thin version: content loss behind HTTP 200. That is the note-block defect at document scale, and it is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate. Rival C converts a loud false alarm into a silent wrong-value generator. Provenance delivers C's entire benefit without C's cost.

Why the winner won
Provenance is the only option that removes the false alarms WITHOUT creating a silent loss, requires no storage migration, and leaves kill-the-cache fully open as a later wave. It also uses machinery the repo already built and then forgot to wire in - the cheapest possible bold move.

The sharpest attack on the winner

A compile-time renderer digest is only sound if render output depends on the renderer ALONE. It may not. Labels.paper_render_opts/3 threads dataset, style and tenant scope; the label spine performs DB lookups; task_resolver.ex (455 lines) appears to resolve LIVE task state into rendered HTML; StatusVocab and tokens_gen feed the emit. If render output depends on live database state, then rendered != html can differ for reasons that are NEITHER renderer drift NOR block divergence: a referenced task changed status since publish, and the paper 422s. That would mean a whole additional 422 class nobody has seen yet.

How the wave absorbs it
If true, it does not kill the direction - it strengthens it. It would prove the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, making provenance the only workable replacement and forcing the digest to cover render INPUTS as well as render code. This is survey question 1, and the verify fleet must settle it before Decide.

Second attack: the four dead papers were repaired by hand, so no live reproduction survives. The wave therefore needs a synthetic, deterministic harness - write a paper, freeze a cache rendered by a prior renderer, read it - that shows 422 BEFORE the fix and 200 AFTER. Anything less is a vacuous green.

The finding under the finding

But the byte-compare is doing DOUBLE DUTY, and that conflation is the real defect. It cannot tell apart two completely different situations:

  • DRIFT - the cache was rendered from THESE blocks by an OLDER renderer. Harmless. Self-healable. The blocks are canonical and re-rendering them is strictly safe.
  • DIVERGENCE - the stored HTML carries content the blocks do not (a legacy paper with rich body_html and a thin-but-not-hollow blocks list). Genuinely ambiguous. Preferring blocks here would silently destroy content.

The 422 was built for case 2. It fires on case 1 because a byte-compare has no way to ask which one it is looking at.
