The code says so in its own comment at 223-226. writer.ex:492-538 has the mirror shape on the generic mutate path: maybe_sanitize_paper_body_html can rewrite body_html without touching the stamp.

Today this is harmless by accident, because the reader ignores the stamp and the byte-compare still catches the record. But the moment the reader trusts 'stamp not equal to current digest therefore drift therefore serve from blocks and overwrite the cache', a renderer-version bump AFTER such a write converts a genuinely DIVERGENT record into an apparent drift - and the reader silently regenerates from the stale blocks, destroying deliberately-supplied content behind HTTP 200. That is precisely the failure class this cycle exists to eliminate, and my winning direction would introduce it. A write-side companion that CLEARS the stamp on any body_html write not derived from the current blocks is therefore MANDATORY scope, not optional polish. mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html already has this exposure today, independent of any reader change.

What lowers the stakes - the divergence class is empirically empty

Every real firing of this gate on record was DRIFT, never divergence: 53 papers caught when the fence first deployed (all 'reconciled through the canonical publish path'), plus the 3 on 07-20, all fixed by clearing body_html and republishing - the drift resolution. If any had been divergence, republishing from blocks would have reported content loss; the epic's own zero-tolerance content-loss counter stayed at zero across 885+ observations. The only test of the divergence branch is a synthetic hand-built fixture. The gate was introduced as adversarial-review hardening (commit 755cff204), not as a fix for an observed incident.

This resolves two things at once. It confirms Rival C's cost is theoretical rather than observed - but 'never seen' is not 'cannot happen', the branch is reachable, and provenance keeps the fail-closed branch for free, so we still keep it. And it lowers the practical severity of the lying stamp (a lying stamp can only lose content on a record that IS divergent, and none are known to exist) while RAISING the relative severity of the resolver-drift class, because that is the one that actually fires.

The rehydration sweep is not a solved prerequisite

  • It has never been run in production. Direct evidence: the 07-20 incident's papers were hand-repaired by clear-and-republish rather than by running the sweep it exists to serve. No workflow, deploy script, or ops doc invokes it anywhere in the tree.
  • It is not paper-scoped and has no status filter - it sweeps EVERY document of any type carrying blocks plus body_html, drafts included, via one unbatched Repo.all with no dry-run and no scoping flags.
  • Render.render_blocks/2 runs unrescued inside the reduce, so one bad row aborts the whole sweep with no checkpoint - a real risk for a first full-corpus run right after four renderer rounds.
  • It writes via raw Repo.update, bypassing Content's broadcast layer and any plugin before_save hooks.
  • Its staleness check is ORDINAL (sv >= current). A hash digest has no ordering, so this must become equality in the same change - and on cutover every existing row reads as non-current, making the sweep's noop fast-path go cold across the entire corpus at once.

The repair family around the P0

note is not a one-off. The census found three severity tiers across compose.ex's clauses (about 40, more than the 30 estimated - article-mode emitters live in components.ex/data_viz.ex/slots.ex, not compose.ex).

TIER 1
Silent total loss. note (body maps to the legacy flat key 'text', never 'content'), callout (empty body when authored with 'text' or 'body'), card - the WORST - and pipeline (partial, per node).
CARD
Bigger blast radius than note. Slots.legacy_slot/2 (slots.ex:187-225) special-cases only callout, note and stage; card falls to the catch-all and gets []. ANY flat-authored card - not merely a misnamed field - renders a completely empty div.bp-card. It deserves equal or higher priority than note in the census.
TIER 2
Visible but misleading. stat/stats/heatmap/chart share an empty(kind) placeholder; task-board says 'No tasks yet'; table renders an empty shell; figure degrades to a bare caption. Loud, but indistinguishable from genuinely-empty.
TIER 3
Safe, and the reference shape. stage, notes and terminal all tolerate flat scalars. stage's explicit legacy fallback (slots.ex:215-223) is what note and card should copy.

The validation seam already exists and needs no new module or doc card. Slots.ex already carries TWO per-type declaration surfaces (slot_decls/1 at 111-146, query_decl/1 at 162-170), and Constraints.validate/2 (constraints.ex:106-129) already aggregates Slots-sourced per-block errors and is live-wired into the publish/patch path at template.ex:213 and patch.ex:378/383. The fix is a THIRD declaration plus a THIRD append - additive, in-fence, and it dodges the 7-card cap entirely.

Premise corrections - four briefs were wrong, including mine

  • 419 published papers today, not 416. The audit's own inventory read 416 two and a half hours earlier; the gap is most likely ordinary corpus growth but was not id-diffed.
  • Move 3's target list is smaller than assumed. Only THREE workflows carry a schedule: trigger - paper-readers, codebase-intel (drift-guard job) and renew-mail-cert. aesthetics-guard, astro-finder-drift, deploy-harnesses and security are push/PR-only and out of scope for 'nightly gate goes red'. Separately: renew-mail-cert has ZERO failure handling of any kind, which means a failed monthly TLS renewal has about 90 days of silent runway.
  • The oauth flake pointers were wrong. oauth_test.exs:77/85 (verify_state) touch only the sandboxed oauth_states table and are immune - a surveyor PROVED this by racing a config mutation against a live verify_state call and getting :ok. The real flake is router_oauth_test.exs, caused by oauth_test.exs:33-44 doing a NODE-GLOBAL Application.put_env(:barkpark_cloud, OAuth, blank-creds) under async:true while another async module calls fetch_identity, which reads that config at call time and returns :provider_not_enabled. Reproduced causally: error during the window, ok after restore.
  • The pr-task-gate rule is NOT in the yml near line 104 (that is the hotfix lane's task-creation literal). It is scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91-92. It also compounds with a lease-lapse deadlock: claim.ex:26 restricts claiming to open|blocked, so an in_progress task whose lease expired is UNCLAIMABLE - the gate demands a recovery action the ledger's own API structurally refuses. Both are already filed; this cycle diagnoses only, since every file involved sits outside the surface fence.

Coverage map - and what NO surveyor reached

CHECKED AND FOUND: papers.ex reader path; all six body_html_sv write sites; render.ex/render/*.ex/slots.ex purity and call graph; labels.ex + codelists.ex resolver closures; document.ex changeset; three test-freeze recipes; compose.ex/components.ex/data_viz.ex/slots.ex field coverage; constraints.ex/tiers.ex/patch.ex/authoring_wall.ex validation seams; all 32 workflow files; pr-task-gate.yml/.sh; claim.ex/queue.ex/pulse.ex; the rehydrate mix task; the live 419-paper corpus; three GitHub Actions runs.

CHECKED AND NOT FOUND - absences that are decisions in waiting: NO test anywhere exercises the stale-sv-carryover scenario, and cloud/test/ has ZERO body_html_sv coverage at all, so the write-side fix is greenfield in the fenced test directory. NO fixture in audit-paper-readers-test.sh simulates a 422 status, so 'the audit detects a 422' rests on live incident history rather than a re-runnable test. NO composite action exists in the repo (.github/actions/ does not exist) and the CI task-filing logic is inline bash in exactly one workflow, not a shared script. NO prior ledger entry proposes a digest-derived render version - Move 1 is genuinely new ground. NO ordering guarantee protects the rehydrate task's ordinal comparison against a hash. NO surveyor found any Slack/Discord notify channel anywhere.

CORNERS NO SURVEYOR REACHED: the /3 theme-aware EMAIL render variants (cards_email.ex, fleet_email.ex, panels_email.ex and the DataViz email twins) were never audited for the same field-name fragility, though compose.ex:126-183 routes every non-article style through them. The release-gate paper source controller behind /release-gates/:id/papers/:role/source was never traced server-side - unknown whether it shares reader_source. ShareLinkController's LIVE static fallback (share_link_controller.ex:61,298-316) reads body_html with NO drift check at all and is untouched by the P0 plan - arguably its own wrong-value generator. apply_document_block_op/5 (block_ops.ex:811) was never traced against the stamp. No surveyor swept barkpark_web/ or plugins/ for ad-hoc Repo writes to content[body_html]. And chart_html/1's exact consumed keys were never read.

§

Verify plan - the last look before the plan is cut

Ten assignments. This round does not browse; it closes the unknowns Decide cannot proceed without. Every load-bearing claim must be PROVEN by running something - a test that can fail, a compile, a live query - not by reading. Models are chosen so that Opus carries anything where being wrong is expensive.

V1
Resolver-drift false positives - opus, worktree. THE CRUX. Prove or refute that renaming a referenced doc or editing a codelist label makes an unedited paper 422. Runs a real test through reader_source, and counts live published papers carrying field-reference or codelist blocks. If this bites, the P0 slice must widen beyond the digest.
V2
The lying stamp - opus, worktree. Prove by running that a verbatim/legacy body_html write leaves a stale sv beside new HTML, then show whether the proposed classification rule misclassifies it as drift. Determines whether the write-side clear is mandatory co-scope.
V3
Corpus census - sonnet. Re-earn 419 vs 416 by id-diff, size the resolver-bearing block population, and confirm the 11 no-stamp both-fields papers are the whole fail-closed class. Live queries, not inference.
V4
Reproduction harness - opus, worktree. Write and RUN the drift repro: freeze a cache with a lagging stamp, show 422 today. Must be demonstrated able to fail. No republish anywhere in the recipe.
V5
Digest feasibility - sonnet, worktree. Compile a throwaway digest twice in different build dirs and prove byte-identical; touch one render file and prove it changes; and prove the rehydrate task's ordinal sv >= current actually breaks on a string.
V6
Card and note silent-empty - sonnet. Run a test proving a flat-authored card renders an empty shell at 200, and query the live corpus for any published paper carrying a flat card or a content-keyed note. Upgrades card from theoretical to confirmed, or not.
V7
CI filing credentials - opus. Probe live whether BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN can actually create a task in the workspace/project paper-readers would file into. Ungreppable; Move 3 is vapor if it cannot.
V8
Validation seam is live - opus, worktree. Prove by running that an error appended in Constraints.validate/2 actually blocks a publish with a non-200, rather than being swallowed. The whole slot-coverage contract rests on this.
V9
OAuth race - sonnet, worktree. Prove the candidate fix closes the race, and prove the existing guard's grep cannot match module-form keys - i.e. that it passes vacuously today.
V10
Audit truth - sonnet. Run the full paper-readers audit end-to-end against production for a fresh earned count, and prove with a fixture that the script actually turns a 422 into a failure.

Wave status: verifying. Decide follows this round, and will set builder_model 'opus' on every slice.

§

Verification results - what the deep round proved, and where it overturned the plan

Ten verifiers flew. Three of them contradicted the strategic direction, and in every case the evidence won. What follows quotes the decisive proof lines rather than summarising them.

PROVEN: the mechanism, and that provenance is unread

conflicting_html_cache?/4 (papers.ex:129-138) byte-compares a fresh render against the stored HTML and never reads content[body_html_sv] - grep returns zero occurrences of the stamp anywhere in papers.ex. Six writers, zero readers. Stronger than the grep, a behavioural sweep over sv values [absent, nil, 1, 2, 3, 99] proved all six produce the IDENTICAL 422: 'provenance is NOT consulted: sv=1 and sv=current both give {:error, :ambiguous_source}'. Provenance cannot influence the verdict, rather than merely being absent from the file.

The blast radius is exactly 4 reader_source/3 call sites, all public-reader; Studio is untouched because it reads via get_document/get_paper. A fix inside papers.ex un-breaks five downstream surfaces with zero edits outside the fence.

PROVEN: the digest mechanism, and that the obvious implementation would have been wrong

Two independent builds of identical source gave a byte-identical digest: df438146989a86763ef4c9fd97d022e409fb884e69d7432a424f458e1cb46d24 both times. Appending one byte to render/walk.ex moved it to 58bcc60a8be39e05e4833e02df68f91c3cbede3299821b684f3d0e568eaf5eeb; reverting restored the original exactly.

The near miss A surveyor TESTED the alternative rather than assuming it. :beam_lib.md5/1 is rebuild-stable, but raw whole-.beam MD5 is NOT - it embeds the absolute source path (35E919CE... vs A4AA7823... for two path-only-different builds). A naive 'hash the beam' implementation would have become the permanent false alarm it was meant to prevent.

The covered set was settled by an Erlang trace, not by reading: trace_pattern on Tiers and Constraints while running render_blocks/2 over callout/note/stage/card captured 'Tiers/Constraints calls during render_blocks/2: []'. Both modules stay out. slots.ex stays in.

OVERTURNED (1): the byte-compare has a THIRD failure class nobody named

My own sharpest attack aimed at task_resolver and MISSED - TaskResolver is genuinely pure and resolve_tasks_in_blocks is never called inside the 422 gate. The identical attack then landed through a different door.

Labels.paper_render_opts/3 - the SAME opts builder used by both the cache-write sites and the 422 gate - supplies ref_resolver and codelist_resolver closures that run live Ecto queries. A probe created a referent, authored a field-reference block at it, wrote a byte-exact body_html, stamped the CURRENT version, and confirmed {:blocks, _}. The ONLY subsequent mutation was renaming the REFERENT. reader_source then returned {:error, :ambiguous_source}. Same for a codelist relabel. Mutation-proof on both: 'left: {:blocks, _} / right: {:error, :ambiguous_source}'.

Under the proposed rule - stamp == digest AND bytes differ implies divergence, keep the 422 - that paper is MISCLASSIFIED and hard-fails. This is EXTERNAL REFERENT DRIFT, and neither 'drift' nor 'divergence' covers it. It strengthens the direction rather than killing it: it proves the byte-compare is unsalvageable as a drift detector under ANY versioning scheme, which makes Rival C more dangerous and Rival B useless. But the P0 could not ship as 'derive the digest' alone.

Sized: exactly 1 of 419 published papers carries either block type (portabledoc-showcase), and it is ARMED - sv=3, a 53,077-byte cache with the live-resolved title 'Diagrams that draw themselves in the terminal' baked in, whose referent is itself a published paper. N=1 is a snapshot, not a bound.

OVERTURNED (2): the write path deliberately preserves a lying stamp, and the digest ARMS it

block_ops.ex:208-232 preserves an existing body_html_sv on verbatim body_html writes; its own comment at :223-226 says this is deliberate. Harmless today only because the reader ignores the stamp. A probe drove the real upsert path and produced a persisted record classified three ways:

  • TODAY -> {:error, :ambiguous_source} - 422, safe
  • RULE @ v3 (stamp == current) -> :divergence_keep_422 - 422, safe
  • RULE @ v4 (stamp != current) -> :drift_serve_blocks_and_overwrite - 200, and 'CONTENT LOSS: 52 bytes discarded behind HTTP 200'
Why two correct fixes are dangerous together Nothing about the record changes between rows 2 and 3. The only mover is the renderer version - which the digest slice makes move on EVERY renderer commit. Move 1 and Move 2 are individually sound and jointly load a gun. The write-side stamp clear became mandatory co-scope, not polish.

The remedy is Map.delete, not a sentinel: a sentinel is by construction != current, so it routes straight into the overwrite branch - fail-open by discipline. Control proved Map.delete holds: ':unknown_fail_closed' at BOTH v3 and v4. And it must key on is_binary(attrs[body_html]), NOT on not is_list(blocks) - the pure carry-over leg produces a fully coherent record (reader => :blocks), so a blanket delete would manufacture new false 422s.

A hazard nobody had flagged also surfaced: the writer persists a CALLER-SUPPLIED stamp verbatim ('[no-blocks attrs] persisted sv = 1'). Under the new rule that is a client-controlled classification switch.

OVERTURNED (3): the validation seam the plan named is dead for 416 of 419 papers

Constraints.validate/2 IS live and blocking - an injected error returned 409 halted, fail-closed. But Template.validate/1 wraps the whole thing in 'if Enum.any?(blocks, &locked?/1)', and its own docstring says 'Papers with no locked blocks pass untouched'. Live census: 3 papers carry a locked block, 416 do not, and of the papers containing note or card blocks, ZERO are locked. Proven end-to-end: the identical injected error rejects a publish on a locked paper and returns HTTP 200 on an unlocked one.

The patch path is dead through a second door - its before-valid guard only vetoes when the doc was already valid, which legacy papers never are. The seam to use is block_ops' unconditional with-chain beside reject_hollow_result.

The rule shape was measured, not argued: across all 419 papers the NARROW rule flags 5 blocks with ZERO false alarms (all verified genuine by rendering); a positive allowlist flags 38, ~33 of them legal chrome. And 9 slot-shaped blocks across 6 published papers are silently dropping prose right now - this is not hypothetical.

PROVEN: the alerting remedy would itself have been a wrong-value generator

BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN does not exist in ANY scope - 5 repo secrets, none of them it; all 6 deployment environments empty; org secrets structurally impossible because FRIKKern is a user account (orgs/FRIKKern/actions/secrets 404s). Three workflows already reference it and have been silently degrading since they were written.

The remedy was the same defect class Even WITH a token, the shape we would have copied files an invisible task. The exact createIfNotExists body was run against production: HTTP 200, and the response is '"_id":"drafts.probe-ci-filing-DELETEME","_draft":true'. It creates a DRAFT, absent from the published ledger that bp task ready reads - while the workflow prints 'Filed override task'. Copying it would have shipped a nightly alert that files nothing and says it worked.

Hence the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, which needs no provisioning. Separately: the audit's 422 detection was proven REAL and non-vacuous - the real script exits 1 with the paper in .failures[], and the same script with the status gate removed exits 0 reporting ok:true on the identical fault.

Coverage, including the not-founds

  • NOT FOUND, and it matters: paper-readers.yml has zero matches for notify|issue|slack|failure() - confirmed independently by three verifiers.
  • NOT FOUND: mutations.ex contains no body_html reference - the patch path is not a second carry-over source. The lie has exactly ONE source.
  • NOT FOUND: no prior art implementing a render digest - 1254 search hits, no duplicate build to reconcile with.
  • NOT FOUND: 0 flat-authored cards and 0 content-keyed note items in the live corpus - the note/card class is reachable and proven at the render layer, but currently EMPTY in production, which is why it ranks below the P0.
  • NOT REACHED: ShareLinkController's static fallback (it reads body_html with no drift check at all) and the /3 email render variants. Filed as backlog, not silently dropped.
  • PREMISE CORRECTED: 419 published papers, not 416 - and the 3-paper gap is pure post-audit growth, proven by publish timestamps 2h after the audit run completed. Only THREE workflows are actually scheduled.
  • PREMISE CORRECTED twice by verifiers against their own first pass: body_html and body_html_sv are TOP-LEVEL envelope keys; a census keyed on content[...] reports a false all-zero.
§

Decisions

The full set with reasons is the epic's memory at .claude/workflows/bp-production-truth-charter.md (D1-D31), committed. This Paper carries the wave's story; the charter carries the epic's. They must not fork. The load-bearing ones:

  • D4/D5 - derive the renderer version as a compile-time sha256 over sorted SOURCE TEXT, never a .beam hash: proven rebuild-stable and change-sensitive, where the beam hash was proven unstable.
  • D8 - stamp != digest is drift (serve blocks); stamp == digest with differing bytes is divergence (keep the 422); no stamp fails closed: removes the false-alarm class while preserving the safety property exactly.
  • D9 - resolver-dependent blocks are exempt from the byte-compare: their bytes are a function of external state the blocks never claimed to pin, so they cannot evidence divergence in either direction.
  • D10 - do NOT freeze resolved labels: a frozen label makes 'stamp matches' true while the correct rendering legitimately differs, serving the OLD title.
  • D12/D13/D14 - clear the stamp on the verbatim leg only, via Map.delete and never a sentinel: absent is already fail-closed; a sentinel is fail-open by construction.
  • D16/D17 - the sweep compares by equality and SKIPS the divergent class: otherwise the stamp clear trades a read-path loss for a sweep-path loss.
  • D19 - alert via the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, not a bp task: the task token does not exist and the mutation shape files a draft while reporting success.
  • D22/D23/D24 - narrow rule, blocking write-side ratchet, wired into the unconditional seam: 0 false alarms vs ~33, and the named seam is skipped by 416 of 419 papers.
  • D27 - the fence is extended to the three scheduled workflows, two scripts and the rehydrate mix task: the fence exists to avoid the Studio and PDS epics, and none of these belong to either.
§

Wave plan - what is in flight

Seven slices, every builder on opus (Fable is spend-limited this cycle). Rounds are law: round 2 slices are NOT dispatched this run - the lead dispatches them after their dependencies merge, because a round-1 slice with an unmerged dependency burns a builder to produce a BLOCKED report.

Round 1 - dependency-free, building now

  • pt-w1-renderer-source-digest (medium, portable_doc/render* + the mix task) - derive the version, cut the stamp over to a digest, convert the sweep comparison to equality. Gate: cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark/portable_doc/ test/barkpark/papers/body_html_render_version_test.exs
  • pt-w1-write-side-stamp-honesty (medium, content/papers/block_ops.ex + content/writer.ex) - clear the stamp on verbatim writes, strip caller-supplied stamps. Gate: mix test test/barkpark/content/papers_reader_source_test.exs test/barkpark/portable_doc/
  • pt-w1-scheduled-gate-alerting (medium, .github/workflows/ + scripts/) - all three scheduled workflows file a GitHub issue on failure via one shared, hermetically tested script; plus a permanent 422 fixture for the audit. Gate: bash scripts/file-ci-failure-issue.test.sh && bash scripts/audit-paper-readers-test.sh
  • cloud-oauth-replay-test-is-seed-flaky (small, cloud/test/) - extract the blank-creds test to an async:false module and add OAuth to the guard's shared-seam keys. Gate: cd cloud && mix test the oauth surface at --seed 1 and --seed 424242

Round 2 - deferred, dispatched after dependencies merge

  • pt-w1-reader-provenance-classification (large, content/papers.ex) - AFTER the digest AND the stamp honesty merge. The reader consults provenance and exempts resolver-dependent blocks.
  • pt-w1-rehydrate-sweep-hardening (medium, the mix task) - AFTER the digest merges. Divergent-class skip, dry-run, batching, a rescue around the render.
  • pd-note-block-silent-content-loss (medium, portable_doc/slots.ex + block_ops.ex) - AFTER the stamp honesty merges, because both edit block_ops.ex. The slot-coverage contract, proven at note and card.

Backlog filed rather than left as anecdote: pt-backlog-sharelink-static-fallback-no-drift-check, pt-backlog-kill-the-body-html-cache, pt-backlog-block-field-census, pt-backlog-renderer-digest-dependency-gap. A duplicate GitHub-orphan filing was deleted in favour of the existing spd-b45-deleted-task-orphans-github-mirror.

The standing bar METHOD LAW on every slice: a republish-based mutation can never prove a cache path, because publish regenerates the cache and silently overwrites the probe. Assert STATE, not exit codes, and demonstrate every assertion able to fail.
